rounds.text: Jay Bharat Maruti Ltd trades at a compelling discount, with a P/E of 12.6x and an EV/EBITDA of 7.88x that sit well below sector benchmarks of 25.2x and 12.91x respectively [E1, E6, E11]. Profitability is robust and outperforming historical valuation levels, demonstrated by a 5-year compounded profit growth of 39% and a TTM profit surge of 349%, alongside strong returns including an ROE of 22.1% and ROCE of 16.4% [E13, E12, E19, E21]. Operational efficiency is highlighted by expanding operating margins reaching 11% in Mar 2026 and solid cash generation, with operating cash flow hitting Rs 197 Cr and a cash conversion ratio of 1.43x [E30, E34, E35]. Furthermore, a sharp 64.3% reduction in Capital Work in Progress to Rs 110 Cr indicates that heavy recent capex is successfully completing, paving the way for new capacity to come online [E40]. Conceded: the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends read inconsistent over the last two periods, and 3-year compounded sales growth is muted at 3% [E16, E32, E33].

Despite recent profit acceleration, the structural top-line growth for Jay Bharat Maruti Ltd remains weak, evidenced by a compounded sales growth of just 3% over three years [E16] and a poor 11.2% over five years [E62]. Institutional participation is retreating rather than endorsing the rally, marked by foreign holdings dropping from 3.71% to 1.31% [E42] and scanX flagging negative money flow alongside decelerating earnings growth [E44, E70]. Furthermore, the operating margin trend is explicitly flagged as inconsistent over the last two years and two quarters [E32, E33], while historical profitability has been subdued with a low median return on equity of 11% over 10 years [E26] and 11.8% over the last 3 years [E64]. Investors also face extreme volatility risks, highlighted by an annualised volatility of 53.0% [E54] and a severe historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -86.3% [E53]. Conceded: the company trades at a modest P/E of 12.6x [E1] alongside a strong one-year price return of 123% [E25] and recent robust cash conversion [E34].

Conceded: compounded sales growth over three years is 3% [E16] and median return on equity over 10 years is 11% [E26]. However, focusing solely on past three-year sales overlooks that trailing twelve-month sales growth has rebounded to 11% [E17], profit growth has surged by 39% over five years and 349% over the trailing twelve-month period [E19, E21], and operating margins have expanded to 11% in March 2026 compared to 7% three years earlier [E30]. Conceded: foreign institutional holdings have declined [E42] and operating margins are flagged as inconsistent over short two-year intervals [E32, E33], but these institutional flows are overshadowed by a rules-based screen score of 87 out of 100 [E65] and a fundamental backdrop where profit growth vastly outpaces 1-year price growth by 226% [E57]. Conceded: historical volatility and drawdowns are high [E53, E54], yet today the stock trades at an attractive P/E of 12.6x—substantially below the sector benchmark of 25.2x—while backed by robust operating cash flows of Rs 197 Cr and a sharp 64.3% reduction in capital work in progress indicating that new capacity is successfully coming online [E1, E6, E35, E40].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month sales growth has rebounded to 11% [E17], profit growth reached 39% over five years and 349% over the trailing twelve-month period [E19, E21], and operating cash flow reached Rs 197 Cr with capital work in progress down 64.3% [E35, E40]. However, the bull's reliance on these recent figures masks severe structural vulnerabilities, including a poor 3-year compounded sales growth of just 3% [E16] and a long-term 5-year sales growth of only 11.2% that Screener flags as poor [E62]. Furthermore, the bull minimizes the persistent institutional exodus, which features foreign institutional holdings declining from 3.71% to 1.31% and active negative money flow [E42, E44], alongside a specific screen warning that earnings growth is decelerating [E70]. The bull also downplays that the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are explicitly flagged as inconsistent over the last two periods [E32, E33], while the company carries a low 3-year average return on equity of 11.8% [E64]. Finally, pointing to a P/E of 12.6x [E1] ignores the extreme historical volatility of 53.0% and a catastrophic worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -86.3% [E53, E54] that expose investors to severe downside risks.
